lines.text: How a bank checks a card payment for fraud while you wait.
On a Saturday night, a woman buys a gift on her phone.
No shop assistant can see her card.
The bank's fraud team cannot check every card payment as it happens.
Fraud is found only after the money has gone.
A model scores the payment in under a fifth of a second.
It reads how she paid and her account's past.
Almost all payments pass. Those in doubt are held for a person.
The most worrying go first.
An analyst spots a payment made with stolen card details and stops it.
A person, not the model, makes the call.
Tonight's weekend shopping does not match what the model was last tuned on.
Honest payments are held, and the queue grows.
At a month-end peak, the check ran past its time limit.
A data job slowed the store the model reads from.
Can shoppers trust a fraud check that stops honest payments by mistake?
She is still waiting.
No payment is blocked until a person has looked at it.
The analyst finds nothing wrong and lets her payment through.
Each analyst's yes or no is kept for the next re-tune.
Weekly checks track false alarms, missed fraud and the queue.
In May, the board accepted some false alarms and set a check each quarter.
Weekend false alarms are not fixed yet.
The goal is fraud stopped as you pay, with a person behind every block.
Every scene is taken from its AI Canvas and its records.
